caption: The drawing depicts a wooden double door set in an arched stone doorway. The doors are vertically aligned, each with a wavy grain pattern, and are colored in a muted brownish-red shade. The arched doorway is constructed from large stone blocks rendered in shades of light tan and ochre. The door frame features two columns on either side, each with a base and capital, and both the columns and arch show signs of age and wear, with patches of coloring indicating weathering or paint chipping. Below the door, there is an area of stone or brick threshold transitioning to a tiled floor, with the tiles depicted in reddish and brownish hues laid out diagonally. The background is a light beige, blank wall with minimal detail. Near the bottom right of the drawing, the artist's signature "Ralph J. de Treville" is visible in small, brownish-red print.
title: Doorway and Doors
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
